payload.body: Contact quotient (Cn) is a voice-quality parameter quantifying the fraction of the fundamental period T0 during which the vocal folds are in contact in voiced phonation. From the electroglottographic signal (EGG) or glottal-flow waveform g(n), the contact phase is the interval during which the signal indicates vocal fold contact, and Cn = contact phase / T0. Parameters: (1) the electroglottographic or glottal-flow signal estimated per voiced frame, (2) the fundamental period T0 from pitch tracking, (3) the contact-phase extraction method (EGG derivative zero crossings or glottal-flow extrema). It is reported as a dimensionless ratio; the maintained reference range for typical phonation sits near 0.5-0.7, and an elevated contact quotient indicates prolonged vocal fold contact as in pressed or hypofunctional phonation. Persistence mechanism: the standardized clinical voice-quality parameter computed by voice-analysis software (Praat, laryngology suites) from the glottogram, taught in voice-disorder curricula, and revised as the standard; it persists as a maintained member of the voice-quality measurement map. [formal: quotientia contactus | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.body: Period perturbation is a class of voice-quality parameters that quantify the cycle-to-cycle variation in the fundamental period of voiced speech. The general measure computes the normalized difference between consecutive periods: given N consecutive glottal cycles with periods P_i, perturbation = normalized deviation of |P_{i+1} - P_i| relative to the mean period. Named variants include: APQ1 (average absolute difference quotient), JRR (jitter ratio), and JDP (jitter absolute difference). Parameters: (1) the voiced speech signal, (2) the pitch-synchronous segmentation at cycle boundaries, (3) the specific perturbation variant formula. Reported in percent or absolute units (ms). Persistence mechanism: maintained as a measurement class by the discipline of laryngology and speech science; implemented in voice-analysis toolkits (Praat, laryngology suites), taught in voice-disorder curricula, and standardized in clinical practice. [formal: perturbatio periodica | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

Period perturbation is a class of voice-quality parameters that quantify the cycle-to-cycle variation in the fundamental period of voiced speech. The general measure computes the normalized difference between consecutive periods: given N consecutive glottal cycles with periods P_i, perturbation = normalized deviation of |P_{i+1} - P_i| relative to the mean period. Named variants include: APQ1 (average absolute difference quotient), JRR (jitter ratio), and JDP (jitter absolute difference). Parameters: (1) the voiced speech signal, (2) the pitch-synchronous segmentation at cycle boundaries, (3) the specific perturbation variant formula. Reported in percent or absolute units (ms). Persistence mechanism: maintained as a measurement class by the discipline of laryngology and speech science; implemented in voice-analysis toolkits (Praat, laryngology suites), taught in voice-disorder curricula, and standardized in clinical practice. payload.scope: A human-made voice-quality measurement category quantifying cycle-to-cycle variations in the amplitude (energy) of voiced speech, built to persist as a standardized measurement class in speech science and laryngology for voice-disorder assessment.

payload.name: amplitude-perturbation
payload.scope: A human-made voice-quality measurement category quantifying cycle-to-cycle variations in the amplitude (energy) of voiced speech, built to persist as a standardized measurement class in speech science and laryngology for voice-disorder assessment.

payload.body: Amplitude perturbation is a class of voice-quality parameters that quantify the cycle-to-cycle variation in the amplitude (energy level) of voiced speech. The general measure computes the normalized difference between consecutive cycle amplitudes: given N consecutive glottal cycles with amplitudes A_i, perturbation = normalized deviation of |A_{i+1} - A_i| relative to the mean amplitude. Named variants include: APQ3 (average absolute difference quotient over 3-cycle windows) and the standard deviation variant (standard deviation of cycle amplitudes divided by their mean). Parameters: (1) the voiced speech signal, (2) the pitch-synchronous segmentation at cycle boundaries, (3) the specific perturbation variant formula. Reported in percent or decibels (20*log10(std/mean)). Persistence mechanism: maintained as a measurement class by the discipline of laryngology and speech science; implemented in voice-analysis toolkits (Praat, laryngology suites), taught in voice-disorder curricula, and standardized in clinical practice. [formal: perturbatio amplitude | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.note: Pinned sense: INSTANCE_OF tests whether contact-quotient is a specific named member of the voice-quality family. The voice-quality definition carves the family as 'a fixed, named set maintained as the measurement map of voice-disorder assessment' and explicitly lists 'source-contact measures derived from electroglottography (contact quotient, open quotient)' as members. Contact quotient IS one of these named members, computed as contact phase / T0 with its own standardized reporting unit and maintained reference range. Nearest kind is voice-quality itself — same pattern as jitter, shimmer, open-quotient, closure-quotient each filing INSTANCE_OF→ voice-quality.

Pinned sense: Cn = contact phase / T0, where the contact phase is the interval indicated by the electroglottographic (EGG) signal — the definition names the EGG or glottal-flow signal as its input and EGG-derivative zero crossings as its extraction method. Remove-the-target test: electroglottography is the measurement technique that produces the glottal-contact time series (voltage envelope inversely proportional to contact area); without it there is no EGG signal, no contact-phase extraction, and no Cn value. The direct operand anchor is electroglottography, not glottal-flow: the EGG modality is the one pinned for contact-phase estimation (its impedance physics — high when open, low when in contact — is why EGG contact outlasts flow closure and why Cn's maintained range 0.5-0.7 differs from closure quotient's 0.3-0.5). This is the mirror of the accepted family pattern open-quotient/closure-quotient DEPENDS_ON glottal-flow, where each quotient anchors to the signal it is computed from.
